messages.author: 7aa24f8fd9c3bc7e
messages.subject: Areal downscaling (disaggregation)
parts:
Dear INLA users/team,


I was wondering whether it's possible to use the R-INLA package for disaggregating areal data, namely counts.

For the sake of discussion, let $\mathcal{D}$ be the study area with spatial support consisting of $M$ non-overlapping regions, $\left\{ \mathcal{R}_{m} \right\}_{m=1}^{M}$, where $y_{m}$ denotes the observed count of $\mathcal{R}_{m}$.

The ultimate goal is to estimate the \textit{latent} counts, say $\widetilde{Y}_{n}$, corresponding to $N$ non-overlapping regions comprising a finer and misaligned spatial support, $\left\{ \mathcal{S}_{n} \right\}_{n=1}^{N}$.

Within a hierarchical framework, if $\widetilde{Y}_{n}$ is assumed to have a Poisson distribution with intensity rate $\lambda_{n}$:
$$\widetilde{Y}_{n}\mid \lambda_{n} \sim Poisson (A_{n}\lambda_{n}),$$
where $A_{n}$ is the area of $\mathcal{S}_{n}$ and $\log(\lambda_{n})=Z_{n1}\beta_{1}+\ldots+Z_{nP}\beta_{P}+U_{n}$
with $Z_{np}$ the measurement of covariate $Z_{p}$ and $U_{n}$ the spatial effect associated to $\mathcal{S}_{n}$. In this case,
$${Y}_{m} \sim Poisson(\sum_{n:\mathcal{S}_{n}\cap\mathcal{R}_{m}\neq\emptyset}A_{mn}\lambda_{n}),$$
where $A_{mn}$ is the area of $\mathcal{S}_{n}\cap\mathcal{R}_{m}$.

Further, the prior for the set of spatial effects $\mathbf{U}$ is an IGMRF with `precision matrix' $\kappa\mathbf{W}$, where $\mathbf{W}$ is the adjacency matrix of regions $\mathcal{S}_{n}$. A fully Bayesian hierarchical model is set by specifying a multivariate normal prior for the fixed effects $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ and a Gamma hyperprior for the precision parameter $\kappa$.

Is there a way to fit this model via the inla function?


Best wishes,
Roman.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Areal downscaling (disaggregation)
parts:
Hi Roman,

since the observation model takes the form Po(\sum_j \exp(\eta_{ij})) instead of Po(\eta_i), INLA can't do this model directly (although some have approximated it as Po(\exp(\sum_j \eta_{ij})), which isn't the same thing). We are however working on related model structures that can be implemented using the additional linearisation step in the inlabru package, which will allow this type of model. It requires some updates to the inlabru interface to allow dissimilar size of inputs and observations, that I plan to work on after my current student coursework marking period is finished.

Finn

Finn

Best,
Roman.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Areal downscaling (disaggregation)
parts:
Hi,

the current implementation of the R-INLA package has certain restrictions on the structure of the link between latent variables and observations; essentially, it supports generalised additive model structures, and the
log(lambda_i) = log(sum_j(log(eta_{ji}))
doesn't follow that restriction.
The INLA method itself doesn't necessarily require that restriction though; one can write down the theory for such models using the same derivative calculations, but it's more difficult to implement more general model families.
Inlabru gets around that by linearising the predictor and iteratively calling INLA. This yields the correct posterior mode for the estimates, but approximates some of the posterior dependency structure further than a full INLA implementation would do.

As to one-to-one vs one-to-many, that is not an issue. One observation depending on multiple latent variables is the by far modest common case, which includes simple "fixed effects" and spatial models, and _any_ additive model structure
The key is that for standard additive models, the latent variables are _added_, and the only non-linearity is the link function in the final step to conditionally independent observations.
Your model has an additional final step that breaks that structure, so the R-INLA implementation doesn't know how to deal with it (but inlabru does, though the interface needs some improvements before it's practical).

Finn
